description: Single-axes engineering stress–strain plot (y-axis "Engineering stress (MPa)", 300–1000 in 100 MPa steps; x-axis "Engineering strain (%)", 0–80 in 10% steps) overlaying seven colour-coded curves for five steels and their heat treatments. Three black curves, Fe-8.5Mn-5.6Al-0.3C [51]: "800°C/1min" shows a small yield drop near 830 MPa, rises to the highest peak of the figure (just below the 900 MPa gridline, around 15% strain) and fractures near 33%; "800°C/30min" peaks lower (~790 MPa) and also ends near 33%; "900°C/30min" yields ~630 MPa and reaches a long, near-flat plateau of ~720–730 MPa extending to ~76% strain. Two blue curves, Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C [44]: solid "800°C/5min" peaks ~620 MPa and fails near 15% strain; dashed "800°C/5min+400°C/10min" holds ~610 MPa out to ~27% strain. Two red curves, 850°C/5min [41]: Fe-8.1Al peaks ~510 MPa, Fe-6.8Al peaks ~450 MPa, both with 15–30% elongation. The panel demonstrates the strength–ductility trade-off: ferritic Fe-Al steels are weakest and least ductile, whereas ferrite-based duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steels span 600–900 MPa at 30–76% elongation. No numeric data labels are printed; values are read from gridlines.

subfigures.description: One engineering stress–strain plot with seven overlaid curves in three colours. Black: Fe-8.5Mn-5.6Al-0.3C [51] at 800°C/1min (peak ~890 MPa, fracture ~33%), 800°C/30min (peak ~790 MPa, ends ~33%) and 900°C/30min (yield ~630 MPa, plateau ~720–730 MPa to ~76%). Blue: Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C [44], solid 800°C/5min (peak ~620 MPa, fails ~15%) and dashed 800°C/5min+400°C/10min (~610 MPa plateau to ~27%). Red: Fe-8.1Al (~510 MPa peak) and Fe-6.8Al (~450 MPa peak), both 850°C/5min [41].

observations.observation: The group is a single engineering stress–strain plot with y-axis 'Engineering stress (MPa)' spanning 300–1000 in 100 MPa increments and x-axis 'Engineering strain (%)' spanning 0–80 in 10% increments.
Seven curves are drawn in three colours (three black, two blue, two red), each carrying an in-place text label naming steel composition and heat treatment.
The black curve labelled '900°C/30min [51]' (Fe-8.5Mn-5.6Al-0.3C) reaches by far the largest strain, about 76%, on a near-flat plateau of ~720–730 MPa.

The black curve labelled '800°C/1min [51]' attains the highest stress of the figure — a peak just below the 900 MPa gridline at roughly 15% strain — and shows a small yield-point drop near 830 MPa at low strain.

The two blue Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C [44] curves are both bounded by ~600–625 MPa, but the dashed '800°C/5min+400°C/10min' curve extends to about 27% strain while the solid '800°C/5min' curve terminates near 15% strain.
The two red curves (850°C/5min [41]) are the lowest in strength: Fe-8.1Al peaks at about 510 MPa and Fe-6.8Al at about 450 MPa, both terminating somewhere between roughly 25% and 32% strain.
No numerical data labels are printed on any curve; all values must be read off the axis gridlines.

The caption states the figure shows engineering stress–strain curves of two ferritic steels (Fe-6.8Al and Fe-8.1Al [41]) and two ferrite-based duplex steels (Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C [44] and Fe-8.5Mn-5.6Al-0.3C [51]) after different heat treatments.
The citing text states the Fe-6.8Al and Fe-8.1Al steels yield an UTS of 450–500 MPa and a total elongation (TE) of 15–30%, consistent with the two red curves in the figure.
The citing text states that austempering at 400 °C for 10 min provides a higher elongation for the Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C steel, which matches the longer dashed blue curve in the figure.

The citing text states Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C has δ-ferrite + martensite after annealing at 850 °C and water quenching, but δ-ferrite + bainite + martensite + retained austenite after quenching to 400 °C and austempering for 10 min.

The citing text states Fe-8.5Mn-5.6Al-0.3C has a bimodal structure of clustered austenite particles in a coarse δ-ferrite matrix, with TRIP operative after 800 °C anneals and TRIP plus TWIP after 900 °C/30 min, which the figure's most ductile curve corresponds to.
The citing text states ferrite-based duplex steels can provide a tensile strength of 600–950 MPa with a total elongation of 30–70%, encompassing the black and blue curve ranges in the figure.

Discrepancy: the figure labels the Fe-3.3Mn-6.6Al-0.2C curves '800°C/5min' and '800°C/5min+400°C/10min', whereas the citing text describes the same steel after annealing at 850 °C followed by water quenching or austempering at 400 °C; the two readings are not reconciled.

unreadable_items: No numeric values printed on any curve; all read values are estimated from axis gridlines and are therefore approximate.
The low-strain yield-drop region of the three black curves overlaps closely, so its exact stress level cannot be resolved precisely.
Exact fracture strain endpoints of the red Fe-6.8Al and Fe-8.1Al curves cannot be read more precisely than between the 20% and 30% gridlines.
